title: CISA adds four exploited flaws to KEV: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap
summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 18, citing evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2024-10441 in Synology DiskStation Manager, CVE-2026-40217 in BerriAI LiteLLM (unprotected alternate channel), CVE-2026-90436 in Apache Axis (unsafe reflection) and CVE-2026-90817 in Vanderbilt University REDCap (code injection). The alert gives no fixed versions. The Hacker News reports exploitation including ransomware on Synology NAS, cryptomining and LLMjacking.
plain: The US cyber agency says attackers are actively using four flaws in a Synology NAS system, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and the REDCap research tool.
exec: Four widely deployed products now have confirmed exploitation, so patching deadlines apply for federal agencies and are a good signal for everyone else.
action: Find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist. Axis 1.x is end of life with no fix (migrate or apply the July 12, 2026 commit); keep Axis, LiteLLM and REDCap off the open internet until addressed.

key_findings: Four CVEs added to the KEV catalog based on evidence of active exploitation.
The alert lists vendor, product and vulnerability type but no CVSS scores or fixed versions.
recommendations: Follow BOD 26-04 and apply vendor remediation.

review.note: Compared with CISA alert and The Hacker News: four CVEs, products, active exploitation, severity 3 and KEV due dates match; action fixed because Axis 1.x is end of life with no vendor fix.
